seoTitle: How to Connect a Namecheap Domain to Hostinger Hosting (2026)
metaDescription: Point a domain you bought on Namecheap at Hostinger hosting by updating the nameservers: the exact fields to change, what not to paste, and how long propagation takes.
intro:
Buying a domain on Namecheap and hosting on Hostinger is a common combination, but the two platforms don't talk to each other automatically. You have to tell Namecheap where to send visitors. The fix is one settings change: swapping Namecheap's default nameservers for Hostinger's. It looks intimidating the first time because the two dashboards look nothing alike and the change doesn't take effect instantly, which makes people think they did it wrong.

This guide walks through finding the nameserver values in Hostinger, logging into Namecheap, and making the swap, including the one field people paste too much into, plus what to expect while the change spreads across the internet.
prerequisites: The domain registered and active in your Namecheap account
A Hostinger hosting plan with the domain already added under Websites
Login access to both accounts (the one that owns the domain, not a new signup)

steps.heading: Get your Hostinger nameservers
steps.body:
Before touching Namecheap, grab the nameserver addresses Hostinger wants you to use. Hostinger's own documentation points you to Websites > your site's Dashboard > Hosting plan > Plan Details, where a Nameservers card lists them; some accounts also see them on the domain's own overview panel, formatted the same way as the screenshot below. They're listed as two addresses ending in dns-parking.com, each shown with an IP address in brackets next to it.

Copy only the two nameserver addresses themselves. Namecheap's documentation is explicit that when you're given both nameservers and IP addresses, the IP addresses don't go into the Custom DNS fields; only the ns1/ns2 hostnames do. Keep this tab open, since you'll paste these values into Namecheap in a later step.

image.caption: The nameserver values Hostinger provides for connecting an external domain — two addresses to copy exactly as shown.

steps.heading: Log into your Namecheap account
steps.body: Head to Namecheap and sign in with the account that owns the domain, not a new signup, since creating a second account won't have your domain attached to it. If you're not sure which email you used to register, check your original purchase receipt before trying to reset a password. Once you're in, the dashboard opens to your account overview, and the domain you want to redirect is listed under your active domains.

image.caption: Namecheap's sign-in screen. Use the account that owns the domain; a fresh signup won't have it listed.

steps.heading: Open Domain List and select your domain
steps.body: From the left-hand menu, click Domain List, find the domain you want pointed at Hostinger, and click Manage next to it. This opens the domain's settings page, split into sections for status, privacy protection, PremiumDNS, and further down, Nameservers, which is the one you need. Everything above that section (renewal status, WHOIS privacy) can stay as it is; you're only here to change one dropdown.

image.caption: The Nameservers dropdown on a domain's settings page, showing Namecheap BasicDNS, Namecheap Web Hosting DNS, and Custom DNS.

steps.heading: Switch to Custom DNS and paste in Hostinger's values
steps.body: Click the Nameservers dropdown and choose Custom DNS instead of whatever is currently selected, usually Namecheap BasicDNS by default. This reveals empty fields where you paste the two Hostinger nameservers, one per line, in the ns1.example.tld format, with no extra spaces and no IP addresses. Confirm with the green checkmark that appears next to the field; Namecheap will show a brief confirmation once it saves. Don't add a third or fourth nameserver unless Hostinger specifically gave you one.

steps.heading: Wait out DNS propagation
steps.body: The change doesn't take effect the moment you save it. Both Hostinger and Namecheap's own documentation put propagation at up to 24 hours for local ISPs to pick up the new nameservers, occasionally longer depending on your domain's prior TTL settings. During this window it's normal for the site to load correctly on one network and show an old page or an error on another; that's caching, not a broken setup. Changing the nameserver fields again mid-wait restarts that clock, so leave them alone once they're saved.

steps.heading: Confirm the connection inside Hostinger
steps.body: Once propagation has had time to settle, go back into Hostinger and check the domain's status. It should flip from a pending or unverified state to active, confirming Hostinger can see the nameserver change. If it still shows pending after a full day, double-check the exact nameserver values in Namecheap character by character; a mismatched character in a dns-parking.com address will block the connection without throwing an obvious error. Also worth checking: that an IP address didn't end up pasted into one of the nameserver fields by mistake, since that field only accepts hostnames.

troubleshooting.problem: Hostinger's nameserver panel keeps showing a warning icon next to a current nameserver
troubleshooting.cause: The live nameservers it's detecting still don't match what it's asking for, usually because the Namecheap side hasn't been saved yet or propagation hasn't caught up.
troubleshooting.fix: Re-check that Custom DNS was saved on Namecheap (green checkmark, not just typed in), then allow the propagation window before checking again.

troubleshooting.problem: Email stops arriving after the nameserver switch
troubleshooting.cause: Namecheap's own documentation notes that host records, including MX records for email, aren't carried over automatically when nameservers change.
troubleshooting.fix: Recreate the MX records in Hostinger's DNS zone (or wherever mail is hosted) before or immediately after switching.

troubleshooting.problem: The domain works from one device or network but not another
troubleshooting.cause: Normal DNS caching during the propagation window; different ISPs and devices refresh their DNS cache on their own schedule.
troubleshooting.fix: Check from a different network or an online DNS checker instead of repeatedly re-saving the nameserver fields, which restarts the wait.

faq.question: How long does it take for a domain to connect after changing nameservers?
faq.answer: Both Hostinger and Namecheap document up to 24 hours for most ISPs to pick up the change, occasionally longer. Test from a different network or an online DNS checker if your own connection still shows the old site.

faq.question: Do I need to change anything on the Hostinger side besides adding the domain?
faq.answer: You need the domain added to your Hostinger hosting plan and its nameservers copied correctly into Namecheap. If you'd rather not change nameservers at all, Hostinger also supports pointing a domain via A records, which leaves DNS management with Namecheap.

faq.question: Hostinger shows an IP address next to each nameserver. Do I paste that into Namecheap too?
faq.answer: No. Namecheap's documentation is specific on this: when a provider gives you both nameservers and IP addresses, only the nameserver hostnames (the ns1.dns-parking.com style addresses) go into the Custom DNS fields.

faq.question: Will changing nameservers affect my existing email if I use Namecheap Private Email?
faq.answer: Yes. Switching to Custom DNS hands DNS control to Hostinger, and Namecheap's documentation confirms host records aren't copied over automatically, so any MX records need to be recreated in Hostinger's DNS zone or mail will stop routing.

faq.question: What if the Nameservers dropdown only shows Namecheap options and no Custom DNS?
faq.answer: Custom DNS is a standard option on every Namecheap domain. If it's missing, confirm you're logged into the account that owns the domain and not a linked or shared account with limited permissions.

faq.question: Can I switch back to Namecheap's own DNS later?
faq.answer: Yes, at any time. Return to the same Nameservers dropdown and select Namecheap BasicDNS or Namecheap Web Hosting DNS, though this triggers another propagation wait, and any DNS records set up under Custom DNS won't carry over automatically.
